If they are able to continue their journey, they should do so immediately, ensuring they can drive safely. If the maximum authorised mass does not exceed 3,500 kilograms, and they are travelling at an abnormally low speed, seriously disrupting traffic, they will travel along the right-hand hard shoulder, if passable and wide enough, or, if not, along the essential part of the road. If travelling along a motorway or dual carriageway at an abnormally low speed, they must leave it at the first exit.   
 
(Página 196 del manual 'Learning to drive')

Maneouvres                  
       
9 Immobilisation: Stationary vehicles Detention (Halting)      
9.2 Emergency detention (halting due to an emergency)  
Vehicles that have been involved in an accident or breakdown:
If they are able to continue their journey but need an assistance service, they should leave the traffic lanes as soon as possible and head to the first available exit using the right-hand hard shoulder, regardless of maximum authorised mass.
If they are unable to continue their journey, they must stop on the right-hand hard shoulder or at the place where they cause the least obstruction to traffic, using the left-hand hard shoulder or central reservation if needed.
(Página 196 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help:
11 Crash helmets
 
11.1 Tips for buying a crash helmet
Size of the helmet:
The helmet must be properly fitted to the head. Where there is doubt between two sizes, it is important to choose the one that is more fitted and can be adjusted correctly, since the interior padding usually stretches a little with use. If the rider wears glasses, it is important to try these with the helmet too.
(Página 81 del manual 'Learning to drive')

11 Crash helmets
 
11.1 Tips for buying a crash helmet
Fastening the helmet:
It is important to ensure and verify that the helmet has been fastened correctly. The helmet must stay affixed to the rider’s head in the event of the rider being involved in a collision, or falling off his machine. If the helmet is not properly buckled it will invariably come off during an impact.
(Página 82 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help:
12 Distances
 
12.4 Lateral separation
All drivers when passing or crossing other vehicles and users should always leave a sufficient (side) separation distance so as to avoid any likelihood of danger and potential impact. This is referred to as ‘lateral’ separation.
As a general rule, this lateral separation depends on:
The speed.
The state of the road.
The vehicles that are crossing or passing.
The weather and environmental conditions.
An adequate lateral separation distance should allow sufficient margin both to avoid a dangerous situation from occurring and additionally to allow for any potential steering deviation to correct or realign the vehicle.
 
(Página 180 del manual 'Learning to drive')
